subject: Control-plane heartbeat interruption impacting hosted inference — initial status & steps
raw_thread:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: ops@auroraedge.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 13:11:00 -0800
Subject: Control-plane heartbeat interruption impacting hosted inference — initial status & steps

Hi Alyssa / AuroraEdge SRE team,

We detected a control-plane heartbeat interruption affecting a subset of hosted inference pools starting at ~13:05 PST. Impact observed: intermittent 502/503 responses and elevated p95 generation latency for tokenized generation routes (/v1/generate and /v1/chat/completions).

What we know right now:
- Start: 2026-11-23 13:05 PST
- Symptom: brief heartbeats lost between orchestration layer and a subset of inference hosts leading to routing fallbacks and some duplicated retries
- Scope: ~3% of requests to US-West hosted pools (affecting a small number of customer requests including some of AuroraEdge's traffic)

What we did immediately:
- Activated incident playbook and started routing away from the impacted host pool
- Increased capacity to absorb traffic, disabled the rapid-retry path for the affected routing tier
- Opened an internal trace collection (attached: auroraedge-traces.tar.gz)

Next steps: we are actively triaging root cause and will follow up with a concise status update within 2 hours. If you have request IDs or times where you saw duplicate charges or retries, please share them (we've requested logs on our side too).

Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts production traffic and are prioritizing.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: auroraedge-traces.tar.gz (trace bundle), incident-snapshot-20261123.png (sample error distribution)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Control-plane heartbeat interruption impacting hosted inference — initial status & steps

Team — quick technical note and recommended public wording below. I attached an internal trace extract (ctrlplane-trace-23nov.txt) and a short remediation checklist.

Technical summary (initial):
- Root cause: a transient partition in the control-plane heartbeat channel between the orchestrator and a specific GPU host pool (us-west-pool-7). The orchestrator removed a small set of hosts from active routing while heartbeats were re-established; during that window a subset of requests were re-routed to the fallback path which triggers a fast-retry in the old routing policy.
- Affected endpoints: /v1/generate and /v1/chat/completions in the hosted US-West pools (p95 elevated; small percentage of 502/503s).
- Timeline:
  - 13:05 PST — first heartbeat loss detected
  - 13:07 PST — routing fallback active; elevated p95 and isolated retries observed
  - 13:18 PST — orchestration roll-forward to stable control-plane version; routing normalized
  - 13:25 PST — monitoring shows steady recovery; post-fix traces collected

Actions taken:
- Forced routing away from us-west-pool-7 at 13:08 PST
- Disabled the legacy fast-retry path for the fallback tier at 13:10 PST
- Performed an orchestration rollback/roll-forward to clear stale state; control-plane heartbeats returned by 13:18 PST
- Collected traces and request IDs for affected customers (see attachment)

Customer-facing/statuspage suggested wording (1 paragraph):
"An intermittent control-plane heartbeat disruption affected a small set of hosted inference hosts in US-West between 13:05–13:25 PST on 2026-11-23. Some customers experienced transient 502/503 responses and elevated p95 latency during this window. We mitigated the issue by routing traffic away from the impacted host pool and stabilizing the control-plane; normal service resumed by 13:25 PST. We are continuing a post-incident review and will follow up with a detailed postmortem and any customer impact analysis."

Recommendation on credits: offer a targeted billing credit if we confirm duplicate billed requests resulting from retries — propose 1 day of usage credit for affected customers as a gesture while we complete audit.

Next steps: Jordan — you can send the concise customer-facing note above. We will prepare the postmortem draft (link below) and attach RCA traces.

Marissa Cole
Senior Product Manager, Runtime Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: ctrlplane-trace-23nov.txt (internal trace extract)

Hi Alyssa — follow up with the customer-facing summary and next steps.

Summary (short):
Between 13:05–13:25 PST we experienced an intermittent control-plane heartbeat disruption affecting a small subset of hosted US-West hosts. The disruption caused routing fallbacks which in turn resulted in elevated p95 latency and isolated 502/503 responses for a small percentage of requests to /v1/generate and /v1/chat/completions.

What we did for you:
- Rerouted traffic away from impacted pool (applied at ~13:08 PST)
- Disabled the legacy fast-retry path that amplified retries (applied at ~13:10 PST)
- Stabilized the control-plane via a targeted orchestration roll (stability observed by ~13:18 PST)
- Collected traces and a list of request IDs for affected requests — we will audit billing for duplicates and share results

Links and artifacts:
- Incident status page: https://status.redwood.inference.com/incidents/INC-2026-11-23-ctrlplane-heartbeat
- Postmortem draft (read-only): https://drive.redwood.inference.com/drive/folders/postmortems/2026-11-23-auroraedge-draft

Offer: We will proactively audit your account for duplicate billed requests caused by retries. If duplicates are confirmed we will provide a billing credit (proposed: 1 day usage credit). Please let me know if you prefer an immediate credit while we finalize the audit.

Would you like a 30-minute technical call tomorrow to walk the traces with our reliability team? If so, propose a few times and we'll schedule.

Thanks again for the quick heads-up and patience — we’ll follow up with the full postmortem once complete.

Best,
